title: The Open-Weight Ecosystem & Quantization
summary: Learn how model family, artifact format, quantization scheme, lineage, runtime behavior, and task quality combine to determine whether an open-weight artifact is deployable. The offline lab computes payload and resident-memory estimates from synthetic evidence, then repairs a runtime evidence gate.
objectives: Distinguish model architecture, artifact format, quantization scheme, and runtime behavior without inferring one from another.
Read GGUF metadata and record unsupported lineage, license, or runtime claims as UNKNOWN.
Use measured bits per weight, not a nominal quantization label, to predict tensor payload bytes and separate payload from container overhead.
Distinguish packed artifact size from dense resident weight memory when a runtime dequantizes at load.
Explain why quantizing from an original high-precision checkpoint differs from requantizing an already-quantized artifact.

Run and repair an offline evidence gate that validates inputs, calculates deployment estimates, and holds artifacts with missing evidence, unexplained size discrepancies, insufficient memory, or failed synthetic task scores.

sections.title: Tensor-only files versus self-describing files
paragraphs: A model family, an architecture, and a downloadable artifact are different things. Meta Llama, Qwen, DeepSeek, Mistral, and Microsoft Phi are model-family examples to investigate. NVIDIA Nemotron and Z.ai GLM are additional research candidates. A family name alone establishes no exact architecture, modality, format, runtime compatibility, price, or license grant. Record those facts from evidence for the exact artifact and runtime version, or write UNKNOWN.

Hugging Face documents safetensors as a tensor format and GGUF as a binary format containing tensors plus standardized metadata. GGUF metadata can identify general.architecture, quantization version, majority file type, a license claim, base-model lineage, trained context length, attention head counts, and a chat template. Metadata is evidence about the artifact, not proof that every claim made by its converter is legally or technically correct.

The GGUF filename convention is not reliably machine-parsable. Confirm an artifact using its digest and metadata rather than treating text such as Q4_K_M as proof. If tensors are quantized, the GGUF specification requires general.quantization_version. Deployments can also contain multiple shards or a separate multimodal projector, so inventory the complete artifact set.

Keep four evidence columns separate: artifact evidence describes bytes and metadata; architecture evidence identifies the loader and tensor organization; runtime evidence states whether a documented version keeps that exact scheme packed on the stated hardware; workload evidence records measured quality and resource results. A model card or filename cannot substitute for runtime documentation or a measurement.

code.label: Evidence record for one exact artifact
code.code:
family: Qwen                         # discovery label only
artifactDigest: UNKNOWN              # establish with a cryptographic digest
format: GGUF                         # establish by parsing the file
architecture: UNKNOWN                # read general.architecture
quantizationScheme: Q4_K_M           # scheme label, not exact bpw
measuredBpw: UNKNOWN                 # measure or obtain exact artifact evidence
lineage: UNKNOWN                     # original precision or requantized?
runtimeMode: UNKNOWN                 # packed, dequantized, or UNKNOWN
runtimeEvidence: UNKNOWN             # exact runtime, version, hardware, documentation
licenseClaim: UNKNOWN                # a claim is not legal advice or a new grant

sections.title: Bits per weight is the unit that matters
paragraphs: A quantization label names a storage scheme, not an exact file size. The GGUF documentation describes Q4_K as 256 weights stored in eight blocks, using 144 bytes in total. The arithmetic is 144 bytes × 8 bits ÷ 256 weights = 4.5 bits per weight. Block scales, minima, and mixed tensor types explain why the measured average can exceed the digit in a label.

For an artifact with P parameters and measured average B bits per weight, predicted tensor payload bytes equal P × B ÷ 8. Measured B already includes the scheme's per-block scale and minimum overhead and any tensor-type mixture represented by that average. Do not add those costs again. Container metadata, alignment, tokenizer data, or unexplained bytes can still make the actual file larger.

Worked example from the lab's synthetic fixture: P is 8,000,000,000 weights and B is 8.5 bits per weight. Predicted payload is 8,000,000,000 × 8.5 ÷ 8 = 8,500,000,000 bytes. The synthetic actual file is 8,585,000,000 bytes, so overhead is 85,000,000 bytes and the discrepancy is 1.00 percent of predicted payload. These are fixture values, not measurements of a vendor model.

GB and GiB are different units. One GB is 1,000,000,000 bytes; one GiB is 1,073,741,824 bytes. The worked payload is 8.5 GB, or about 7.916 GiB. Keep calculations in integer bytes and convert only for display.

sections.title: Calibration, importance matrices, and requantization
paragraphs: llama.cpp documents a workflow that first converts an original model to a high-precision GGUF and then quantizes it. Its quantize tool can use an importance matrix to reduce quantization loss. The same documentation warns that --allow-requantize can severely reduce quality compared with quantizing from 16-bit or 32-bit weights. Missing lineage therefore causes a deployment hold in the lab.

Hugging Face groups GPTQ and AWQ as calibration-based methods and bitsandbytes, HQQ, and SINQ as on-the-fly methods. Method names do not establish quality for a particular task. Calibration data, implementation, tensor exceptions, runtime kernels, and the source checkpoint all matter. Measure the exact artifact on representative tasks.

The lab includes synthetic task scores solely to exercise a quality gate. A score of 6 out of 10 against a threshold of 8 fails even when packed weights fit the memory budget. Those values were authored fixtures and are not vendor benchmarks, performance claims, or comparisons among real model families.

code.label: Lineage and quality gate

sections.title: A 4-bit file is not automatically a 4-bit deployment
paragraphs: Packed file size and resident weight memory answer different questions. If a supported runtime kernel consumes the packed blocks directly, the lab estimates resident weights from predicted packed payload bytes. If the runtime dequantizes to a 16-bit dense representation, resident weight bytes equal parameter count × 16 ÷ 8. File-container overhead is not added to either weight estimate.

Hugging Face's dated Transformers GGUF documentation describes a packed Metal/MPS path for Qwen3.5 and Qwen3.5MoE when matching kernels are available. Its fallback and other architectures dequantize GGUF to a dense model at load. This is a runtime-specific statement, not a universal rule for GGUF, Qwen, Metal, CUDA, or future Transformers releases.

For the lab's synthetic 8-billion-parameter Q4-style artifact, measured 4.9 bits per weight predicts 4,900,000,000 packed bytes. Its declared runtime instead dequantizes to 16 bits, so resident weights are 8,000,000,000 × 16 ÷ 8 = 16,000,000,000 bytes. The starter defect incorrectly reports 4,900,000,000 bytes by assuming every runtime stays packed.

If runtime behavior is unsupported, resident memory is UNKNOWN and deployment is held. Do not silently select packed or dense behavior. Also budget activations, key-value cache, runtime workspace, and non-weight components separately in a real capacity plan; this lab intentionally calculates resident weights only.

code.label: Runtime evidence gate to repair

sections.title: Offline lab: repair the resident-memory evidence gate
paragraphs: Offline lab: repair the resident-memory evidence gate in training/self-hosted-and-aiops/open-weights-and-quantization/lab/. The canonical public lab directory is https://github.com/project42dev/project42-content/tree/main/training/self-hosted-and-aiops/open-weights-and-quantization/lab. From the repository root, use Node.js 22 with native ESM and built-in modules: no package installation, network, GPU, model download, or live provider account is required. The lab uses synthetic fixtures to separate exact artifact evidence, architecture evidence, runtime evidence, and workload evidence. Run the immutable tests and baseline report, inspect src/analyze.js, and repair only residentWeightBytesForRuntime. The deliberate defect assumes every runtime keeps quantized weights packed. The repair must return predictedPayloadBytes for packed mode, parameters * denseBits / 8 for dequantized mode, and null for UNKNOWN mode. Do not hardcode fixture IDs, edit tests or fixtures, or replace the learner file with solution/reference.js. After the repair, rerun the tests, assess fixtures/variants.json and fixtures/changed.json, and compare with the reference only after attempting the repair. All model names, byte counts, runtime declarations, memory budgets, and task scores are synthetic teaching data, not provider benchmarks, specifications, prices, or legal grants.

From the repository root, change into the lab directory and run the tests. Node.js 22 native ESM is used. There are no packages to install, and the lab requires no network, GPU, model download, or dependency installation.

First run the immutable tests and the baseline report. Inspect src/analyze.js, then repair only residentWeightBytesForRuntime. Do not replace the learner file with solution/reference.js or hardcode fixture identifiers. Run the tests again, assess fixtures/changed.json, and only then compare your logic with the reference.

All model names, byte counts, runtime modes, and task scores in the fixtures are synthetic. They demonstrate exact arithmetic and evidence handling but are not live execution results or model benchmarks. Real deployment evidence would require parsing the exact artifact, recording its digest and lineage, consulting documentation for the exact runtime version and hardware, and measuring the intended workload.

activity.title: Size, trace, and gate synthetic model variants
instructions: Open README.md and fixtures/variants.json. Confirm that every numeric value and score is labeled synthetic rather than a real provider measurement.
Run node tests/run-tests.js before editing. Record the exact failing tests and exit code.

For worked-q8, independently calculate predicted payload bytes, actual-minus-predicted overhead, discrepancy percent, packed resident weight bytes, and the 10 GiB budget in bytes. Compare your values with the completed worked example.
For learner-q4, calculate packed payload bytes and then calculate dense 16-bit resident weight bytes. Explain why the two numbers differ.

Inspect src/analyze.js and repair only residentWeightBytesForRuntime so packed, dequantized, and UNKNOWN runtime modes follow their evidence. Do not hardcode fixture IDs or copy the complete reference implementation.
Run all tests, then run the CLI against fixtures/variants.json and fixtures/changed.json. Compare commands separately from the exact expected outputs in README.md.
Explain every HOLD: discrepancy greater than 2 percent, lineage UNKNOWN, runtime UNKNOWN, failed synthetic quality threshold, or resident weights exceeding the stated GiB budget.
After documenting your attempt, compare your focused repair with solution/reference.js. If needed, restore the deliberate starter using recovery/analyze.starter.js and try again.

activity.reflectionPrompt: Which variants remain on HOLD after the runtime repair, what independent evidence would clear each hold, and why would fitting packed weights in memory still be insufficient evidence for deployment?

questions.prompt: A synthetic artifact has 8,000,000,000 parameters and a measured average of 4.9 bits per weight. What is its predicted tensor payload?
questions.explanation: 8,000,000,000 × 4.9 ÷ 8 equals 4,900,000,000 bytes. The measured bits per weight already includes represented block overhead and tensor mixtures.

questions.prompt: Why does the GGUF Q4_K type work out to 4.5 bits per weight rather than exactly 4?
choices: Every tensor is duplicated
Its blocks store scales and minima alongside quantized values
The tokenizer counts as model weights
The filename adds half a bit
questions.explanation: The documented Q4_K layout stores quantized values plus scale and minimum information. Its 144 bytes for 256 weights equals 4.5 bits per weight.

questions.prompt: What does llama.cpp document about requantizing an already-quantized artifact with --allow-requantize?
choices: It is lossless
It is required for every k-quant
It can severely reduce quality compared with quantizing from 16-bit or 32-bit weights
It proves that an importance matrix was used
questions.explanation: The quantize tool warns that requantization can severely reduce quality compared with starting from 16-bit or 32-bit weights.

questions.prompt: An 8-billion-parameter artifact is dequantized by its runtime into 16-bit dense weights. What resident weight memory should the lab calculate?
questions.explanation: Dense resident weights are 8,000,000,000 parameters × 16 bits ÷ 8, which equals 16,000,000,000 bytes. Packed artifact size does not control this result.

questions.prompt: What should the gate do when the exact runtime's packed-versus-dequantized behavior lacks evidence?
choices: Assume packed because the file is quantized
Assume 16-bit dense
Return UNKNOWN resident memory and hold deployment
Use the filename's nominal bit count
questions.explanation: Unsupported runtime behavior must remain UNKNOWN. Assuming either packed or dense would turn missing evidence into a fabricated capability claim.

questions.prompt: A synthetic quantized variant fits its memory budget but scores 6 out of 10 against a task threshold of 8. What is the correct result?
choices: READY because memory is the only gate
READY because quantization always preserves quality
HOLD because the synthetic task-quality gate failed
UNKNOWN because integer scores cannot be compared
questions.explanation: Capacity and task quality are independent gates. The variant remains on HOLD even though it fits memory.
